title: Comparative Evaluation of Retreatment Systems in Removing Gutta-Percha and Bioceramic Sealer
author: Marina Mamdoh Kamal Antonyous
materials: Retreatment using XP Endo Retreatment kit I

steps.title: Calculate sample size and groups
steps.instruction: Determine that 15 teeth per group (total 45) give 80 % power at α = 0.05 for an expected effect size of 12 and SD = 10; plan three experimental groups.

steps.title: Collect and select teeth
steps.instruction: Obtain 45 extracted human permanent single‑rooted teeth meeting inclusion criteria: single canal, fully formed apex, straight curvature <10°, root length ≥16 mm after decoronation, no previous endodontic treatment, no cracks, resorption, calcifications, or restorations; exclude teeth with multiple canals, severe curvature, open apex, resorption, previous treatment, or structural defects.

steps.title: Clean and store specimens
steps.instruction: Remove soft tissue mechanically, store teeth in saline solution at 4–8 °C until use, and rinse thoroughly with distilled water before any instrumentation to eliminate residual saline.

steps.title: Standardize root length
steps.instruction: Decoronate each tooth with a diamond disc under water cooling to obtain a 16 mm root length (working segment).

steps.title: Determine working length
steps.instruction: Introduce a size 10 K‑file until its tip is visible at the apical foramen; set the working length 1 mm short of this point.

steps.title: Initial canal preparation and obturation
steps.instruction: Prepare canals to an apical size #40 with .04 taper using rotary NiTi instruments while irrigating continuously with 5.25 % NaOCl; after shaping, perform a final rinse with 17 % EDTA to remove the smear layer; obturate with gutta‑percha cones and WellRoot ST bioceramic sealer using the single‑cone technique; store specimens at 37 °C and 100 % humidity for 7 days to allow complete sealer setting.

steps.title: Randomize specimens into groups
steps.instruction: Generate a random sequence on https://www.random.org for the 45 teeth, allocate 15 to each of the three groups (XP‑Endo, D‑Race, Fanta), place each tooth in a sequentially numbered opaque sealed envelope, and keep the allocation concealed until the day of retreatment.

steps.title: Set up debris collection apparatus
steps.instruction: Weigh each empty Eppendorf tube (caps removed) on an analytical balance and record the baseline weight; attach the tooth to the removed tube cap so that any apically extruded material falls into the tube during retreatment.

steps.title: Retreatment – XP‑Endo group
steps.instruction: Use the DR1 file at 800 rpm and 1.5 N·cm torque to create a starting point in the obturation material; then operate the XP‑Endo Rise Shaper at 1000 rpm and 1 N·cm until the working length or the end of the filling is reached; subsequently run the Finisher R for at least 1 minute; irrigate sequentially with 5.25 % NaOCl, saline, and 17 % EDTA, activating the EDTA by passive ultrasonic irrigation for three cycles of 20 seconds each; if the full working length is not achieved, use small hand files (C‑files or C+‑files); record the time from first file insertion to radiographic confirmation of canal cleanliness; finish with a distilled‑water rinse.

steps.title: Retreatment – D‑Race group
steps.instruction: Insert the D‑Race DR1 instrument (size 30, taper .10, length 15 mm) at 800–1000 rpm with light apical pressure and a brushing motion to clear coronal obstructions and create a solvent path; then use DR2 (size 25, taper .04, length 25 mm) at 400–600 rpm and ≈1.5 N·cm torque to reach the working length and remove material from the apical third; irrigate with 5.25 % NaOCl, saline, and 17 % EDTA using the same ultrasonic activation (3 × 20 s); employ hand C‑files if the working length is not attained; record total retreatment time; finish with distilled water.

steps.title: Retreatment – Fanta group
steps.instruction: Work the Fanta #30 file in the coronal third at 300–350 rpm with 2.0 N·cm torque to establish a straight‑line path; continue with the Fanta #25 (tip 25, taper .08, length 18 mm) under the same motor settings for the middle third; finish with the Fanta #20 (tip 20, taper .07, length 22 mm) at the same speed and torque to remove residual material apically and confirm canal patency; irrigate with 5.25 % NaOCl, saline, and 17 % EDTA activated ultrasonically (3 × 20 s); use hand C‑files if needed; record the time from first file insertion to radiographic confirmation; conclude with a distilled‑water rinse.

steps.title: Weigh extruded debris
steps.instruction: After retreatment, remove the tooth and tube cap, weigh the Eppendorf tube again, and calculate the mass of apically extruded debris by subtracting the pre‑procedure weight.

steps.title: Radiographic verification of cleanliness
steps.instruction: Take a radiograph of each tooth after retreatment; confirm that no visible filling material remains before proceeding to sectioning.

steps.title: Section teeth for surface analysis
steps.instruction: Groove the external root surface with a diamond disc, then split the root longitudinally with a chisel to expose the canal walls without altering the internal surface; divide each specimen into coronal, middle, and apical thirds for standardized evaluation.

steps.title: Capture stereomicroscope images
steps.instruction: Photograph each third under a stereomicroscope at a standardized magnification suitable for quantitative analysis.

steps.title: Quantify residual material with ImageJ
steps.instruction: Import images into ImageJ (NIH, USA); define the total visible canal‑wall area for each third; apply uniform thresholding to identify residual gutta‑percha and/or bioceramic sealer; calculate the percentage of wall area covered by remnants for coronal, middle, and apical thirds.

steps.title: Blind outcome assessment
steps.instruction: Have two trained observers, blinded to group allocation, perform the image analysis independently; resolve discrepancies by consensus.

steps.title: Record data and perform statistics
steps.instruction: Enter all measurements (percentage residual material, extruded debris mass, retreatment time) into statistical software; summarize continuous variables as mean ± SD or median [IQR] depending on distribution; select appropriate inferential tests after assessing normality and variance homogeneity.
